summary: Templeton sits in the oak-studded corridor between Paso Robles and Atascadero along US 101, a stretch of inland San Luis Obispo County where summer highs regularly push into the 90s yet winter nights dip into the low 40s — that 40-plus-degree daily swing is what makes the surrounding vineyards viable and gives the air a dry, almost Mediterranean crispness you don't get on the coast just 25 miles west. With fewer than 8,700 residents spread across about eight square miles, the town is essentially a compact main-street core flanked by ranchettes and newer subdivisions, all of it framed by golden grass hills rolling east toward the Cholame Valley. The commute question is real: there's no major employment cluster here, and most professional jobs mean a drive to San Luis Obispo (roughly 25 minutes south on 101) or Paso Robles, making this functionally a bedroom community despite its agricultural roots in wine grapes, cattle, and grain. A median home value near $783,000 against a median household income of about $114,000 yields a price-to-income ratio around 6.9 — manageable compared to coastal SLO but still steep enough that purchasing typically demands significant savings or equity. With 9.7 hours of daily sunshine on average and a poverty rate under five percent, the tradeoff is clear: genuine small-town quiet on a beautiful inland corridor, paid for with car dependence and distance from the economic engines that fund the mortgage.
